title: TBP and SNAP50 transcription factors bind specifically to the Pr77 promoter sequence from trypanosomatid non-LTR retrotransposons.
authors: Macias, Francisco; Afonso-Lehmann, Raquel; Carreira, Patricia E; Thomas, M Carmen
one_liner_zh: 该文通过EMSA等实验鉴定TBP和SNAP50与锥虫逆转座子Pr77启动子序列的直接结合，属于蛋白质-DNA互作研究，但方法为湿实验验证，缺乏AI或物理模拟建模，故评分为5。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Trypanosomatid genomes are colonized by active and inactive mobile DNA elements, such as LINE, SINE-like, SIDER and DIRE retrotransposons. These elements all share a 77-nucleotide-long sequence at their 5' ends, known as Pr77, which activates transcription, thereby generating abundant unspliced and translatable transcripts. However, transcription factors that mediates this process have still not been reported. METHODS: TATA-binding protein (TBP) and small nuclear RNA-activating protein 50 kDa (SNAP50) recombinant proteins and specific antibodies raised against them were generated. Protein capture assay, electrophoretic mobility-shift assays (EMSA) and EMSA competition assays carried out using these proteins and nuclear proteins of the parasite together to specific DNA sequences used as probes allowed detecting direct interaction of these transcription factors to Pr77 sequence. RESULTS: This study identified TBP and SNAP50 as part of the DNA-protein complex formed by the Pr77 promoter sequence and nuclear proteins of Trypanosoma cruzi. TBP establishes direct and specific contact with the Pr77 sequence, where the DPE and DPE downstream regions are docking sites with preferential binding. TBP binds cooperatively (Hill coefficient = 1.67) to Pr77 and to both strands of the Pr77 sequence, while the conformation of this highly structured sequence is not involved in TBP binding. Direct binding of SNAP50 to the Pr77 sequence is weak and may be mediated by protein-protein interactions through other trypanosomatid nuclear proteins. CONCLUSIONS: Identification of the transcription factors that mediate Pr77 transcription may help to elucidate how these retrotransposons are mobilized within the trypanosomatid genomes and their roles in gene regulation processes in this human parasite.
abstract_zh: 背景：锥虫科基因组中定殖有活跃和不活跃的移动DNA元件，如LINE、SINE样、SIDER和DIRE反转录转座子。这些元件在其5'端均共享一段77核苷酸长的序列，称为Pr77，该序列激活转录，从而产生丰富的未剪接且可翻译的转录本。然而，介导此过程的转录因子尚未见报道。方法：生成了TATA结合蛋白（TBP）和小核RNA激活蛋白50 kDa（SNAP50）重组蛋白及其特异性抗体。利用这些蛋白和寄生虫核蛋白与用作探针的特异性DNA序列进行蛋白质捕获实验、电泳迁移率变动分析（EMSA）及EMSA竞争实验，检测了这些转录因子与Pr77序列的直接相互作用。结果：本研究鉴定出TBP和SNAP50是Pr77启动子序列与克氏锥虫核蛋白形成的DNA-蛋白质复合物的一部分。TBP与Pr77序列建立直接且特异的接触，其中DPE和DPE下游区域是优先结合的对接位点。TBP协同结合（Hill系数=1.67）至Pr77及Pr77序列的两条链，而该高度结构化序列的构象不参与TBP结合。SNAP50与Pr77序列的直接结合较弱，可能通过其他锥虫核蛋白的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用介导。结论：鉴定介导Pr77转录的转录因子可能有助于阐明这些反转录转座子在锥虫科基因组中的动员机制及其在该人类寄生虫基因调控过程中的作用。
